"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: No trials have run yet. The baseline's seeds are bimodal (0.068 three times, 0.258 once), so any single 2-seed difference under about 0.1 could be luck. The default recipe makes only 32 PPO updates (131k steps / 4096 samples per update). For an agent that must learn exact, ordered placements, that is few policy improvements. The likeliest gains are more updates per unit of compute: smaller rollouts give fresher data and more updates, and fewer epochs buy more samples (2 epochs gives about 243k steps). Credit assignment also matters. The +1 exact-build bonus comes at the end of an episode of 8–20 bricks, and gamma 0.95 discounts it heavily. A lower entropy coefficient may also help with 401 actions. This round tests three directions: more updates, more samples with more updates, and a longer horizon with less entropy.
analyses.2: All six round-1 seeds scored exactly 0.0684 (35 of 512 designs). The baseline also gave 0.068 on three of its four seeds. So there is a strong, repeatable plateau, and only seed luck (0.258) has escaped it so far. The plateau is probably a local optimum: the policy greedily fills the obvious target cells but never learns the placement order needed for overhangs, or exact completion. Three changes did not escape it: smaller batches with more updates, fewer epochs with more data, and a longer horizon with lower entropy. Lowering entropy may even make it worse. None of these targeted exploration or the size of each policy step. This round tests the opposite directions, one change at a time from the default recipe: stronger entropy exploration, a higher learning rate, and more PPO epochs (more gradient reuse per sample). Any seed above 0.068 is informative, because the plateau value is so exact.
analyses.3: Five of six default-ish recipes stuck seeds at the 0.068 plateau, which looks like greedy filling that never learns exact finishes. Two changes broke the plateau. A higher learning rate (lr 0.0025) gave 0.219 and 0.520 (mean 0.369), the best so far. Stronger entropy (ent_coef 0.03) gave 0.068 and 0.334, so it helped one seed. Changing the number of updates, epochs or horizon at lr 0.001 did nothing: every seed stayed near 0.07, so with the default learning rate none of these effects can be told apart. The main limit seems to be how far the policy moves within the short, linearly decaying learning-rate schedule. With only 2 seeds, one plateaued seed is still likely. Next: push lr to the 0.003 maximum, combine high lr with extra entropy (the two signals that helped), and test fresher data (more, smaller updates) now that lr is high.
analyses.4: The learning rate is the clearest lever. Every lr-0.001 recipe except one entropy seed stayed at the 0.068 plateau. At lr 0.0025–0.003 all six seeds escaped it (0.20–0.65). Adding entropy 0.02 to lr 0.0025 (r3c2) gave the best and most consistent result, with both seeds at 0.518. Doubling the update count at high lr (r3c3) gave the highest single seed (0.648) and the highest train success, but a weak second seed. lr 0.003 alone is about the same as 0.0025. Two seeds is little evidence: spreads within a trial reach 0.44, so differences under about 0.15 are within noise. For the last round I spend two candidates refining r3c2 by stacking the levers that helped, more updates and the maximum lr. The third tests the horizon at high lr, where it was never tested; r1c3 was hidden by the low-lr plateau. The +1 exact-build bonus comes after 8–20 placements and gamma 0.95 shrinks it heavily.
